topic.title: Hardware-Efficient Neural Computation
topic.overview: Practical neural-network efficiency depends on memory movement, activation storage, operator structure, and hardware utilization as well as arithmetic count. This cluster includes compression, low-precision computation, offloading, rematerialization, and architectures with adjustable computation. Representative methods often preserve learned behavior while changing how the computation is organized or stored.
topic.whyItMatters: A theoretically small network can run slowly if its operators use the device poorly. Measuring throughput and memory alongside predictive quality helps distinguish deployable improvements from reductions that exist only in abstract model statistics.
topic.evolution: Early examples concern specialized processors and GPU-based learning. Later work explores binary weights, compressed activations, and combinations of memory-saving techniques. Recent representatives include structure-preserving compression and implicit visual generators whose inference iteration count can be adjusted, reflecting attention to concrete quality–resource tradeoffs across architectures.
openQuestions: Which efficiency gains transfer across devices and batch sizes?
How can compression preserve per-example behavior, not just aggregate accuracy?
